The language and theme buttons are the same size as Login and Add to Discord, and on a big window the whole bar is drawn bigger (and a bit wider) with the page instead of staying small. The point of light of the glass used to be placed by the width of the window, so on a wide screen it was far from the pointer; now it is measured on the bar and glides after the mouse.

entries.title: Status page: every shard in color, with its details when you point at it
entries.summary: Each shard card of the status page now has the color of its ping: green up to 50 ms, yellow from 51 to 150, orange from 151 to 300, and red above that or when the shard is offline. A small legend sits above the cards. Point at a card (or tap it on a phone) to see its servers, its members, its ping and state, and the name and place of the instance that holds it. The search of a server also says which instance has it.

entries.title: Footer: Powered by CubePath and Discloud
entries.summary: The bottom of every page of the site now says that Petto runs on CubePath and Discloud, with a link to each one, in English, Spanish and Portuguese. They are the two places where the bot lives now.

entries.title: Status, totals and the @ stats channels now count every shard
entries.summary: Petto now runs in three places with six shards, and some numbers only saw the first one: the status page said the other shards were offline and counted 86 servers, and the channels of servers and members in the support server said 87. Now every instance reports its own shards (with their members and the name of the instance), and the status page, the public totals, the ranking and the carousel of the home page, the channels of @ stats, /bot info and the verify page count all of the servers. /ping now says the real shard of your server. The cleanup of servers Petto left can no longer take a server of another shard for one that was left.

entries.title: /about: who Petto is, in one card
entries.summary: The new /about command (and !about) shows the bot (its version, how long it has been online, the servers and members of all its shards and how many clusters run them), the server where you used it (owner, members, channels, roles, when it was created, and the shard and instance that look after it), where Petto is hosted (CubePath and Discloud, with a link to each) and five buttons: website, support server, status, add Petto and Premium. It speaks English, Spanish and Portuguese.

entries.title: Credits: CubePath and Discloud are named as sponsors
entries.summary: The credits text no longer says that none of the companies is a sponsor: it now says that CubePath and Discloud sponsor the hosting of Petto, with our thanks, and that the other companies are only credited. It is in English, Spanish and Portuguese. In the bot, /bot info no longer has a button to GitHub, because the code is not open anymore: it has the support server instead.

entries.title: The status messages of the team channels now show every shard
entries.summary: The messages of the status channels still showed only the two shards of the first host, with its own servers and cached members (104 servers, 22,988 members). Now, with the three instances running, they list all six shards with their state, servers, ping and the name and place of the instance that holds each one, and the servers and members of the whole bot. A shard that stops reporting for five minutes is shown as down, and the public status only says that everything is fine when all the shards are running.

entries.title: Alerts when a shard of another server of Petto goes down
entries.summary: Petto now runs in three places, and the status channel only heard the first one. Now every minute Petto checks what each place reports: if a shard stops being ready, or its whole host goes silent for two minutes, the channel says which shard it is, where it runs and how many servers it holds, and it says again when it is back and what is still down. A short reconnect of a few seconds is not announced, and while one is down the public status shows a partial outage.

entries.title: The member count of Petto no longer drops and bounces
entries.summary: The members of the whole bot showed about 90,000 instead of about 135,000, and the number jumped up and down. No server was lost: Petto is still in the same 281. It was a counting mistake after the bot started running in three places. Now each place reports its own numbers every few seconds and they are added up, so the count matches the status page and stays steady. The warning about the servers cleanup is also said once instead of every minute, and the servers carousel logs what it reads from the other places.
